title: Soft coherent radiation, resolution and inclusive cancellation

items.title: Independent soft-radiation resolution model

references.title: Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations, full lecture notes
references.locator: §§5.3–5.6, PDF pp. 19–21; symmetric Fock sectors and the tensor product law for Fock spaces.

references.title: Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt, Quantum Optics, Lecture 5
references.locator: PDF pp. 1–2, equations (1)–(8) and “Photon statistics of coherent states”; normalized coherent-state number weights.

items.statement:
Use SI quantities with $c>0$ in m s$^{-1}$, $\hbar>0$ in J s,
$e>0$ in C, and $\mu_0>0$ in H m$^{-1}$. Let $g=e\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}>0$
be dimensionless. Let $I$ be a finite, possibly empty, set of leg labels.
For each $i\in I$, choose an energy $E_i>0$ in J, a dimensionless velocity
$v_i\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|v_i|<1$, a dimensionless charge number
$Q_i\in\mathbb R$ (physical charge $eQ_i$ in C), and an orientation
$\eta_i\in\{-1,1\}$, where $-1$
denotes an incoming leg and $+1$ an outgoing leg. Assume charge balance
$\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i=0$. Write $h=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$ and
$h(a,b)=a^0b^0-\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b$.

For $n\in S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$, set
$$p_i=E_i(1,v_i),\qquad q=\hbar\nu(1,n),\qquad J(q)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\frac{p_i}{h(p_i,q)},\qquad K(n)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\frac{(1,v_i)}{1-v_i\cdot n}.$$
Here $\nu>0$ is angular frequency in s$^{-1}$ and $\hbar\nu$ is photon
energy in J. The data make $h(p_i,q)=E_i\hbar\nu(1-v_i\cdot n)>0$ and
$J(q)=K(n)/(\hbar\nu)$. The balance condition gives
$h(J(q),q)=0$; this is the conservation convention for this prescribed
eikonal current in the model.

Let $A\subseteq S^2$ be a Borel angular acceptance region and let $d\Omega$
be Euclidean chart surface measure. Write $K(n)=(K^0(n),\mathbf K(n))$ and
define $K_\perp(n)=(I_3-nn^T)\mathbf K(n)$, where $I_3$ is the $3\times3$
identity matrix, and
$$b(n)=\mathbf1_A(n)\frac{gK_\perp(n)}{\sqrt{2(2\pi)^3}},\qquad C=\int_{S^2}|b(n)|^2\,d\Omega(n)\ge0.$$
Thus $b$ and $C$ are dimensionless.

For fixed angular-frequency cutoffs $0<\varepsilon<\Delta<\Lambda$, define
$\nu(\mathbf k)=c|\mathbf k|$ in s$^{-1}$. The one-particle coherent
displacement is the transverse mode function
$$f_{\varepsilon,\Lambda}(\mathbf k)= \mathbf1_{\{\varepsilon<\nu(\mathbf k)<\Lambda\}}|\mathbf k|^{-3/2} {}\times b\!\left(\frac{\mathbf k}{|\mathbf k|}\right) \quad(\mathbf k\ne0), \qquad f_{\varepsilon,\Lambda}(0)=0.$$
The function $f_{\varepsilon,\Lambda}$ has units m$^{3/2}$ in
$L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3)$; the associated free one-photon
energy is $\hbar\nu(\mathbf k)=\hbar c|\mathbf k|$ in J. Define its
exponential vector and normalized coherent vector by
$$\epsilon(f)=\bigoplus_{m=0}^{\infty}\frac{f^{\otimes_s m}}{\sqrt{m!}}, \qquad \Psi_{\varepsilon,\Lambda} =\exp\!\left(-\frac{\|f_{\varepsilon,\Lambda}\|^2}{2}\right) \epsilon(f_{\varepsilon,\Lambda}),$$
where $f^{\otimes_s0}=1$ in the vacuum sector. For a finite partition
$B_1,\ldots,B_r$ of $(\varepsilon,\Lambda)$ into disjoint Borel intervals,
let
$H_j=\{u\in\mathcal H_T:u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ a.e. unless }\nu(\mathbf k)\in B_j\}$.
For a tuple $(m_1,\ldots,m_r)\in\mathbb N_0^r$, its occupation subspace is
the closed span of symmetrized tensors with exactly $m_j$ one-particle factors
in $H_j$ for each $j$ and no factors outside $\bigoplus_jH_j$. The model
defines $N(B_j)=m_j$ on this occupation subspace and assigns it probability
equal to the squared norm of the projection of $\Psi_{\varepsilon,\Lambda}$
onto the subspace. Its resolution parameter
$\Delta$ divides $(\varepsilon,\Lambda)$ into the unresolved band
$(\varepsilon,\Delta)$ and the resolved band $[\Delta,\Lambda)$. The
threshold frequency is assigned to the resolved band; its exact assignment
does not change any $L^2$ vector or probability because a single frequency
has zero one-particle measure.
This is a finite-cutoff free coherent-state model; it does not posit a
detector response or an interacting QED scattering law.

items.title: Orthogonal frequency bands in the coherent soft model have independent Poisson counts

references.title: Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations, full lecture notes
references.locator: §§5.3–5.6, PDF pp. 19–21; symmetric Fock sectors and the tensor product law for Fock spaces. The local proof gives the exact band-occupancy calculation.

references.title: Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt, Quantum Optics, Lecture 5
references.locator: PDF pp. 1–2, equations (1)–(8) and “Photon statistics of coherent states”; single-mode Poisson weights.

items.statement:
Fix the finite-leg current data and cutoffs of the resolved-soft model. For every
finite partition $B_1,\ldots,B_r$ of $(\varepsilon,\Lambda)$ into disjoint
Borel frequency intervals, the coherent state
$\Psi_{\varepsilon,\Lambda}$ has independent band counts. For each $j$,
$N(B_j)$ has Poisson distribution with mean
$$\lambda_j=C\int_{B_j}\frac{d\nu}{\nu},$$
where $\nu$ is angular frequency in s$^{-1}$. Thus
$\lambda_j=C\log(b_j/a_j)$ for an interval with endpoints
$0<a_j<b_j$; endpoint conventions do not matter because $d\nu/\nu$
assigns a singleton zero measure. For $C=0$ every band count is zero.
The model's marked frequency density is the one-particle coherent
intensity $|b(n)|^2\,d\Omega(n)\,d\nu/\nu$.

items.title: Summing unresolved coherent emissions removes the lower cutoff

references.title: Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations, full lecture notes
references.locator: §§5.3–5.6, PDF pp. 19–21; the local argument proves the finite-band coherent count identity.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-posted draft
references.locator: Chapter 26, printed pp. 167–171; detector resolution and the distinction between exclusive and unresolved final states in a different scalar-field calculation. It is context only, not a QED cancellation proof.

items.statement:
In the defined finite-cutoff coherent model, let
$0<\varepsilon<\Delta<\Lambda$ and $C\ge0$. Let $N_u$ and $N_r$ be the
counts in the unresolved band
$(\varepsilon,\Delta)$ and resolved band $[\Delta,\Lambda)$,
respectively. The exclusive no-emission probability is
$$\mathbb P(N_u=0,N_r=0)= \exp\!\left(-C\log\frac{\Lambda}{\varepsilon}\right).$$
For every $n\in\mathbb N_0$,
$$\mathbb P(N_u=n,N_r=0)= \exp\!\left(-C\log\frac{\Lambda}{\varepsilon}\right) \frac{\left(C\log\frac{\Delta}{\varepsilon}\right)^n}{n!}.$$
Summing over all unresolved counts gives the finite-resolution inclusive
probability
$$\mathbb P(N_r=0)= \exp\!\left(-C\log\frac{\Lambda}{\Delta}\right),$$
which is independent of the lower cutoff $\varepsilon$. This is an exact
identity in the defined free coherent model; it does not assert real–virtual
cancellation in interacting QED or a detector's empirical response.

items.title: Photon number divergence can coexist with finite soft energy

references.title: Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations, full lecture notes
references.locator: §§5.3–5.6, PDF pp. 19–21; bosonic Fock sectors and second quantization. The local proof derives the cutoff expectation.

references.title: Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt, Quantum Optics, Lecture 5
references.locator: PDF pp. 1–2, equations (1)–(8) and “Photon statistics of coherent states”; single-mode Poisson weights.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-posted draft
references.locator: Chapter 26, printed pp. 167–170; finite resolution and unresolved states in a different scalar-field calculation. No QED energy formula is imported.

items.statement:
In the defined coherent model, put
$f_{\varepsilon,\Delta}
=\mathbf1_{\{\varepsilon<\nu(\mathbf k)<\Delta\}}f_{\varepsilon,\Lambda}$
and
$\Psi_{\varepsilon,\Delta}
=\exp(-\|f_{\varepsilon,\Delta}\|^2/2)\epsilon(f_{\varepsilon,\Delta})$,
the normalized coherent Fock vector on the unresolved band
$(\varepsilon,\Delta)$.
For $C\ge0$ its mean band count and free-photon energy expectation are
$$\mathbb E_{\Psi_{\varepsilon,\Delta}}N_{(\varepsilon,\Delta)} =C\log\frac{\Delta}{\varepsilon},\qquad \Psi_{\varepsilon,\Delta}\in D(H_\gamma),\qquad \langle\Psi_{\varepsilon,\Delta},H_\gamma\Psi_{\varepsilon,\Delta}\rangle =\hbar C(\Delta-\varepsilon),$$
where $H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|\mathbf k|)$ and $\nu=c|\mathbf k|$ is
angular frequency. If $C>0$, the mean number diverges as
$\varepsilon\downarrow0$, while the energy expectation remains bounded by
$\hbar C\Delta$ and tends to $\hbar C\Delta$. The one-particle displacement
has $\|f_{\varepsilon,\Delta}\|^2=C\log(\Delta/\varepsilon)$ and has no
limit in one-particle Hilbert norm as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. This is an
exact free coherent-state model statement; it asserts no empirical photon
statistics, no interacting QED limit, and no implication about convergence
of a different physical state.

title: Soft coherent radiation, resolution and inclusive cancellation — Examples

items.title: Detector resolution changes a finite inclusive event

references.title: Jan Dereziński, Introduction to Representations of the Canonical Commutation and Anticommutation Relations, full lecture notes
Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt, Quantum Optics, Lecture 5
references.locator: PDF pp. 1–2, equations (1)–(8) and “Photon statistics of coherent states”; coherent-state Poisson number weights.

items.statement:
In the finite-cutoff coherent model, fix $C>0$ and
$0<\varepsilon<\Delta<\Lambda$. The probability of no resolved emission is
$$P(\Delta)=\exp\!\left(-C\log\frac{\Lambda}{\Delta}\right).$$
For any two thresholds $\Delta_1<\Delta_2$ in $(\varepsilon,\Lambda)$,
$P(\Delta_1)<P(\Delta_2)$. This is an exact model law, not a reported
detector count or an empirical estimate.
